what_an_impression_proves: an impression proves the URL was indexed, so the count above is a FLOOR on indexed pages. Zero impressions proves nothing about index state: an indexed page that never ranks high enough to be seen reports zero, which is why the not-indexed columns stay UNAVAILABLE.
how_to_supply_it: URL Inspection API, one call per URL, 2,000/day/property: write each batch to data/atlas/measurements/gsc/url-inspection-YYYY-MM-DD.json as {"rows": [...]} with url, coverageState, lastCrawlTime, googleCanonical, userCanonical, verdict.
Or export Search Console > Indexing > Pages > any row > Export, and save as data/atlas/measurements/gsc/index-coverage-YYYY-MM-DD.csv with URL and Coverage state columns.
Crawl and indexation latency need first_published per URL in reports/atlas/live-production.json; without it the dates have nothing to subtract from and the two latency columns stay UNAVAILABLE.

the_bar_is_a_decision_not_a_measurement.coverage_means: the share of a family's live URLs for which Search Console returned an index state

decision_states.INDEX_STATE_MISSING_VISIBILITY_MEASURED: Search Analytics covers the URLs and index state does not. A family here has a measured visibility answer and an unmeasured indexation answer.
decision_states.SCALE: assign only on complete evidence and an agreed indexed-share bar
decision_states.HOLD: assign only on complete evidence and an agreed bar
decision_states.FIX: assign only on complete evidence and an agreed bar
decision_states.EVIDENCE_MISSING: no GSC state for any URL in this family
decision_states.EVIDENCE_PARTIAL: some URLs have a state, not all
decision_states.READY_TO_CLASSIFY: every published URL has a state; the bar is a decision, not a measurement, so this script stops here

historical_context_different_url_set.what_this_is: The Page Indexing (Pages) report as it stood on 2026-09-21, transcribed from reports/gsc-baseline-2026-09-21.md, which recorded it from the Search Console UI by hand.
historical_context_different_url_set.why_it_is_kept_separate_from_the_cohort: It covers a DIFFERENT URL SET: the 91 core, destination, region and guide pages that were live then. The 500 Atlas pages this analysis is about were published afterwards and are not in these counts. It is historical context for how Google treats this property, not index state for the cohort, and nothing may read it as the cohort's status.
historical_context_different_url_set.source: manual reading of the Search Console interface, not an API call and not an export
redirect_and_duplicate_urls: www.livdar.com/ (www redirects to the apex, expected)

performance_at_the_time.note: both windows give the same totals because every impression fell on 18 and 19 September 2026

historical_context_different_url_set.the_technical_state_at_the_time: all 91 URLs returned 200, were index,follow, canonical to themselves and present in the sitemap, and 30 were indexed. The baseline's own conclusion was that the first bottleneck is indexing rather than titles or CTR.
historical_context_different_url_set.what_that_reason_means: Google knows the URL exists and has chosen not to spend crawl budget on it yet. It is a discovery and priority signal about the property, not a verdict on the page's content, and it is the reason 58 of the 64 not-indexed URLs carried.
historical_context_different_url_set.the_follow_up_this_file_is_owed: the baseline asked to be re-read on or after 2026-10-05 and compared. That re-read has not happened and is what scripts/atlas/gsc-url-inspection.mjs and scripts/atlas/analysis/import-gsc-pages-report.py exist to supply.
